newsitem.title: CANADA: BioChem up on more drug response news.
newsitem.headline: BioChem up on more drug response news.

text.p: BioChem Pharma Inc shares spiked in Toronto on the news that its potential liver disease treatment Lamivudine may be more effective than anticipated, BioChem spokeswoman Christine Lennon said on Friday.
The Montreal-based biotechnology firm saw stock jump 8.70 to 62.80 on light turnover.

Data from a study of Lamivudine showed a correlation between length of treatment and participant response. The information was in an abstract mailed to participants of the upcoming American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases conference, Lennon said.
The annual conference is held in Chicago every November.
"I think essentially the market has taken this as very encouraging," Lennon said.
The abstract landed on people's desks this week, Lennon said, prompting the stock move.

The new information was taken from an extended Phase II study of Lamivudine, an antiviral treatment which is in its final stages of pre-registration clinical testing. Lamivudine works to block the liver disease Hepatitis B, Lennon said. An estimated 340 million people world-wide are chronic carriers, most of whom are in Asia.
BioChem shares climbed closer to a year high of 69.75 a share, nearly double of a year low of 36.50.
"That's a significant move," said Yorkton Securities analyst Ezra Lwowski.
Biotechnology firm Glaxo Wellcome Plc is the exclusive licensee of Lamivudine.
